items.demand_letter:
We represent the class of customers affected by the regional outage OPS-0007, specifically regarding the March service month. On 2026-04-08, your company issued a decision for this period that did not align with the calculations mandated by your own written policy.

The relevant provision is MSA-SCH4 L-4.1. This clause governs the credit amount due for service interruptions and dictates the specific computation method for affected service months.

Your records indicate that a credit of 14,400.0 was applied or decided for the March service month. However, executing MSA-SCH4 L-4.1 against the same facts produces a required credit amount of 24,000.0.

The difference between your decision and the policy requirement is 9,600.0 per customer service-month. This shortfall represents a breach of the agreed terms for every customer to whom this clause was applied in the same manner.

We seek payment of the outstanding difference of 9,600.0 per affected customer service-month. This amount is derived strictly from your own policy computations, not our estimation.

Please remit the total class difference by 2026-05-08. Failure to resolve this discrepancy will leave us no choice but to pursue further remedies.

items.headline: C-8.1 read literally pays a Grade 5+ employee 1.25x for an overtime hour the company pays nothing for
items.why: C-8.1 is drafted as a free-standing precedence rule: where two or more provisions of C-4, C-5 or C-7 would apply to the same hour, "only the single highest applicable multiplier applies". For a Grade 5 employee working the 45th hour, two provisions bear on the hour. C-4.1 would give 1.25. C-5.1 gives nil. The highest of those is 1.25, so on C-8.1's own words the employee is paid 1.25 and C-5.1 is displaced. The company's encoding takes the opposite view, reading C-5.1's opening words "by way of exception to C-4" as taking it outside C-8.1 altogether -- a construction the Annex nowhere states, and one that has to be implied to stop C-8.1 destroying C-5.1 for every senior employee. The claimant does not need to win that argument outright. The company has to run it, on its own document, against a literal reading, for every overtime hour ever worked by a Grade 5 or above. This is AMB-02 in docs/DOCUMENT-DEFECTS.md, recorded there as an open question and quantified here.

items.amount_basis: multiplier computed as 0.0, contended to be 1.25; difference 1.25 multiple of Base Hourly Rate per an employee-hour, to be multiplied by base_hourly_rate for currency
items.narrative: A Grade 6 Incident Engineer in her third year works her 45th hour of the payroll week. This hour falls during a night shift. It is not a public holiday, nor is it part of a critical incident response. Under the company's own rules, because she is Grade 6, she is deemed 'salaried' and denied overtime pay under C-5.1, accruing only time-off-in-lieu. However, C-6.1 explicitly states the night premium is payable 'in addition to, and not in substitution for' amounts payable under C-4 or C-5. Because C-5.1 denies the *payment* but grants *toil*, and C-6.1 mandates the night premium is additive to the C-5 framework, the company is forced to pay the night premium on top of the base rate, despite having zeroed out the overtime multiplier. The documents create a scenario where the 'exception' (C-5.1) swallows the payment mechanism but leaves the additive premium (C-6) intact, resulting in a payable premium for an hour that otherwise yields no cash overtime.

items.headline: L-4.4 extinguishes a 50% service credit on the company's own view that an invoice is undisputed
items.why: L-4.4 removes the credit entirely where the customer is in arrears of an undisputed invoice for more than 30 days. Whether an invoice is disputed is not defined anywhere in the Agreement and is not a fact the supplier gets to find: a customer who has written to query the invoice will say it was disputed, and the entire credit turns on that one word. In the month this fires the service was below 95% availability, so L-4.3 fixes the credit at 50% of the Monthly Service Charge -- the largest number the Schedule can produce -- and L-4.4 is the only thing standing between the customer and it. The customer's counsel will also pair this with L-1.2, which makes credits the sole financial remedy: a supplier arguing that the credit is barred is arguing that a month at under 95% availability carries no remedy at all, which is the argument that gets a sole-remedy clause looked at hard.
items.amount_basis: credit_payable_percentage computed as 0.0, contended to be 0.5 (the executed value of credit_cap_percentage); difference 0.5 money per a customer service-month
items.narrative: A customer account shows 94.9% availability, triggering the 50% credit under L-4.3. The customer is 31 days in arrears on an undisputed invoice, triggering the exclusion under L-4.4. The documents do not specify which exception prevails. L-4.3 sets the credit to 50%; L-4.4 sets it to 0%. The conflict allows the customer to argue for the 50% credit, as L-4.3 is a specific exception to the cap that also defines the credit amount, while L-4.4 is an exception only to L-4.1. The ambiguity favors the customer in maximizing the credit.

clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
An Employee is entitled to an overtime payment in respect of each hour
worked in excess of 40 hours in a Payroll Week, calculated at 1.25 times the
Base Hourly Rate.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
By way of exception to C-4.1, each hour worked in excess of 48 hours in
a Payroll Week is calculated at 1.5 times the Base Hourly Rate.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
By way of exception to C-4, an Employee of Grade 5 or above is not
entitled to an overtime payment. Such an Employee accrues time off in lieu at
the rate of one hour for each hour worked in excess of 40 hours in a Payroll
Week.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
Notwithstanding C-5.1, an Employee of Grade 5 or above is entitled to
an overtime payment calculated in accordance with C-4 in respect of hours worked
on Critical Incident Response.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
Each hour worked on a Gazetted Public Holiday is calculated at 2.0
times the Base Hourly Rate. This rate is payable in substitution for, and not in
addition to, any amount otherwise payable under C-4.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
By way of exception to C-7.1, where hours worked on a Gazetted Public
Holiday are also hours worked in excess of 48 hours in the Payroll Week, the
applicable rate is the greater of (a) 2.0 times the Base Hourly Rate and (b) the
rate determined under C-4.2 plus 0.25.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
A premium of 0.15 times the Base Hourly Rate is payable in respect of
each Night Hour worked. This premium is payable in addition to, and not in
substitution for, any amount payable under C-4, C-5.2 or C-7.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
By way of exception to C-6.1, the night premium is not payable in
respect of an Employee who receives a standing shift allowance under their
individual contract of employment.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
Where two or more provisions of C-4, C-5 or C-7 would apply to the same
hour, only the single highest applicable multiplier applies to that hour.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
C-8.1 does not apply to the night premium under C-6, which is
cumulative with any multiplier determined under C-4, C-5.2 or C-7.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
The maximum aggregate Service Credit in respect of any Measurement
Period is 30% of the Monthly Service Charge.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
By way of exception to L-4.2, where the Availability Percentage is less
than 95.00%, the maximum aggregate Service Credit in respect of that Measurement
Period is 50% of the Monthly Service Charge and the Service Credit is 50%.
clauses.label: RULE

clauses.body:
By way of exception to L-4.1, no Service Credit is payable in respect of
a Measurement Period in which the Customer is in arrears of any undisputed
invoice for more than 30 days.
